chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: The one who performs i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether in the Mosque or in its houses. And he said: I'tikaf is not valid elsewhere except in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah or in a mosque of the congregation. And the one who performs i'tikaf may not pray in a house other than the mosque in which he has performed i'tikaf, except in Mecca, for he performs i'tikaf in Mecca wherever he wishes because all of it is a sanctuary. And the one who performs i'tikaf does not leave the mosque except for a need.
ai.seo_question: What are the differences between i'tikaf rules in Mecca and other cities according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the juristic distinction between Mecca, where the entire area is a sanctuary allowing i'tikaf in any dwelling, and other cities, which restrict it to specific mosques. It highlights the practical implication that a mu'takif in non-Mecca locations cannot leave their designated mosque except for essential needs, reinforcing the sanctity of the prayer space in those contexts.
